title: staged routing and graceful fallbacks for model-variant deployments
creator: Ava Park
description: Add a staged routing layer and deterministic fallback policies to support canary rollouts, A/B tests, shadow traffic, and automated rollback. This ticket covers the compatibility checks for model variants, region failover behavior, and tiered-capacity fallthrough (e.g., premium -> standard -> fallback models). Goal is safe progressive deployments with automated protection from latency/errors/regressions while preserving cost constraints.
acceptance_criteria: Config schema that expresses a routing policy for a model deployment: canary %, buckets for A/B, shadow targets, and fallback chain ordered by compatibility/cost/latency
Compatibility checker that validates a candidate model variant against production request/response contracts (tokenizer, max_seq_len, input/output fields, function-calling shapes)
Deterministic traffic assignment implemented so experiments are sticky per request owner id / session id and stable across runtime restarts
Region failover implemented: requests routed to preferred region, with automatic failover to secondary region when region-level SLOs are breached
Tiered capacity fallthrough applied: when selected variant is unavailable or overloaded, traffic falls back to configured compatible lower-tier variant with metrics emitted
Shadow traffic delivery for offline evaluation without impacting latencies for primary traffic

Automated rollback policy triggers on combined signal (p50/p95 latency degradation, error-rate spike, output-quality regression measured by eval harness) and performs controlled rollback + notification
End-to-end integration tests and production canary executed (1% -> 5% -> 25% -> 100%) with rollback exercised via automated test and manual QA
Docs and Console UI hooks created: rollout preview, traffic split editor, compatibility warnings, and live fallback telemetry visible in Console
implementation_plan: Week 1: Define routing policy schema and storage (feature flag + deploy config). Build lightweight compatibility checker library and unit tests.
Week 2: Implement deterministic sampler and traffic assignment hooks in request router. Add sticky key mapping and ensure consistent hashing across instances.
Week 3: Integrate shadow traffic path (fire-and-forget replication) into runtime; wire offline eval pipeline consumer to shadow stream.
Week 4: Add fallback chain execution: compatibility lookup -> attempt primary -> on overload/timeout/error invoke fallback -> emit fallback_reason metric.
Week 5: Implement region health checks and failover logic with circuit-breaker semantics; test with synthetic region outages in staging.
Week 6: Implement rollback automation controller: threshold config, alerting integration, and safe reversal steps (traffic shift + canary rollback + notifications).
Week 7: QA, runbook updates, Console integration work, and production canary rollout with monitoring & ops oncall present.
rollout_strategy: Phase 0: Dry-run in staging using shadow traffic for new model variants and measure quality metrics for 48h
Phase 1: Canary 1% traffic for 1h; check latency, error rate, output-quality regression (divergence score) and resource utilization
Phase 2: If Phase1 signals green, expand to 5% for 6h with more traffic patterns and longer-form prompts
Phase 3: Expand to 25% for 24h while running A/B metrics collection and cost delta analysis
Phase 4: 100% cutover with staggered regional switches; final validation and monitor for 72h
Rollback: If any configured trigger fires at any phase, immediately shift new-variant traffic to 0% and route remaining traffic to last known-good variant. Trigger automated post-mortem checklist.
monitoring_and_metrics: Latency p50/p95/p99 per variant and per region
Error rate (5xx and model-level errors) and fallback-rate (percent of requests that hit fallback chains)
Divergence score from offline eval harness for a seeded prompt set (token-level similarity + top-k response agreement)
Cost per 1k tokens per variant and net delta versus baseline
Throughput (req/sec) and queueing times inside runtime batching layer
Region health metrics: capacity utilization, GPU memory pressure, hot-shard rate
Automated rollback triggers: p95 latency increase > 30% over baseline OR error-rate > 2% OR divergence score drop > 5 points
testing_notes: Create unit tests for compatibility checker covering tokenizer mismatches, missing function-call signatures, and schema field mismatches
E2E tests simulate region outage by killing region process group and verify failover path and telemetry
Load tests to validate tiered fallthrough under saturation: ensure fallback doesn't induce cascading overloads
Shadow traffic validation: assert that shadow replication does not increase tail latency for primary requests
Simulate rollback by injecting regression signals into metrics pipeline and verify controller sets traffic to safe variant and posts required alerts
decisions_and_tradeoffs: Decision: Stick to deterministic hashing on request_id or user_id for sticky experiments to guarantee stable exposure, even if it slightly skews statistical independence.
Tradeoff: Prefers conservative fallback chain ordering by API compatibility then latency; this may increase cost if a more expensive compatible model is selected as a first fallback.
Decision: Shadow traffic will be sampled at most 2x production RPS to control eval costs; full traffic replication is prohibitively expensive.
Tradeoff: Automated rollback thresholds are conservative (err on false positive rollback) to prioritize availability over narrow quality gains.
follow_up_tasks: Instrument console to show real-time fallback chain activations and most common fallback reasons
Add RBAC controls over who can create/approve rollout policies and automated rollback thresholds
Add a compatibility registry UI that surfaces warnings when a variant is not fully compatible (tokenizer mismatch etc.)
Run a cross-team tabletop exercise with SRE and Oncall to walk through rollback and multi-region failover scenarios
